screened_out.reason: Makes its own watches (competitor). Its Partner API and MCP only push COROS data out to other apps. Nothing shows it taking in third-party overnight data, so there is no real co-op angle; it is a data source, not a partner (support.coros.com Submit an API Application).
Built only on the Garmin Health API ('Your Garmin Data, Your AI'). The product is single-brand by design, so it has no slot for another device.
A strength-lifting app whose readiness comes only from HealthKit. Vybe would reach it passively through Apple Health, and there is no partner or integration page.
A GPS run tracker with social features. Its listing says only 'supported device and health data when available' and names no wearables. No partner page was found, so the opportunity is unproven.
A free tool from a solo developer that sits on top of Intervals.icu plus Apple/Google Health sync. The partner to target is Intervals.icu, not PaceKeeper.

A lab-testing membership. Its Connected Apps are pre-built in-product syncs (Oura, Fitbit, Apple Health) with no third-party developer API. Its clinical positioning also clashes with Vybe's general-wellness scope.
A camera-based vitals SDK with FDA 510(k) clearance. It competes on HRV sensing rather than consuming wearable data, and its medical clearance sits outside Vybe's general-wellness scope.

Indie app (lifttrackapp.com) built around Garmin Connect workout sync, plus phone tracking and a ChatGPT/Claude connection. Its whole proposition is the Garmin ecosystem, Garmin watches already record overnight HRV, and no other device integration or partner interest was found. Fit <7. Revisit if it adds Apple Health/other devices.

Small AI coach app (App Store id6757655267, hosted on a Firebase app domain) with workouts, food scanning and outfit ideas; no wearable or Apple Health integration found in listings, and no company, partner page or contact beyond the privacy policy. Too thin to prove an opportunity.
New offline-first iPhone lifting log (App Store id6762335584). The listing describes no Apple Health or wearable integration, and no developer site or contact was found. Unverifiable and tiny.

Several unrelated apps share the name (e.g. 'GymLog: AI Workout Tracker' by lghdeveloper, 'GymLog AI: Fitness Coach', a Gymlog calorie app by Khamidjon Egamov). None showed wearable integrations, and I could not tell which one is the Claude directory listing. Identity unverified.

Searches only found The Strength Code (a 1:1 slow-HIT personal-training studio in Burbank, CA, with a booking app) and unrelated MCP repos. No app-level wearable integration, and the directory app's identity is unverified.

Could not identify the app. 'Kynra' results were a Philadelphia tech-events calendar (kynra.ai), a Virginia fitness meetup (KYNRA Collective) and an old B2B AI-training design case study. No product, wearable integration or contact verified.

Beachbody's BODi integrates only with Apple Watch/Apple Health (HR overlay on video). No partner/developer program or recovery/readiness feature found, so there is no concrete entry route. Large company, long route without a proven opening.

The Zumba app supports Wear OS and syncing to third-party tracking apps, and it has a 2024 content partnership with Samsung Health, but that is content distribution, not device data. No readiness/recovery feature and no partner or developer program found; dance classes are a weak fit for an overnight HRV band. Long route, no proven opening.

Booking app for a Toronto boutique gym (Marianatek white-label; there is also an Australian studio app). It is a class scheduler with no data or wearable layer. Could be a local gym-sponsorship lead, not an app partner.

Could not confirm which 'Myo' is the directory app. The candidates are meetmyo.com (AI coach that syncs Apple Health workouts/nutrition/sleep) and MyoAmigo (lifting log with MCP). Both rely on Apple Health only, so Vybe reaches them by writing to HealthKit without a deal. Identity unverified; revisit if the listing is confirmed.

German corporate step-challenge platform (instingo.de, 200+ companies) that syncs steps from Apple Health, Garmin, Fitbit and Samsung Health. Its product is daytime step counts, and nothing shows that an overnight ECG/HRV band contributes steps. Fit <7 unless Vybe adds step counting or instingo adds sleep challenges.

Habit tracker that auto-completes habits from Apple Health (it removed Health Connect on Android in 2024). Vybe would appear automatically by writing sleep to HealthKit, so a partnership adds little. No device-specific integrations or partner program found.
AI photo calorie counter (Veywell / calioai.com); store listings show no wearable or partner program; small clone app, low realistic partner value.
